## Structural feedback

You answer both questions and use an appropriate four-paragraph problem–solution structure. The introduction lists fossil fuels before accidents, but Body 1 reverses that order; matching the roadmap would make progression cleaner. The accident argument is circular because “more cars” simply leads to accidents “naturally,” without using the prompt-specific mechanism of inexperienced first-time drivers on busy roads. Body 2 repeats the fewer-cars idea three times but never explains why an awareness campaign would persuade car owners to change behaviour. Fewer cars would implicitly reduce both accidents and fuel demand, but this two-part result should be stated explicitly. The conclusion covers the task again but restates rather than synthesises. The single highest-impact fix here is rebuilding Body 2 around better public transport → changed behaviour → fewer accidents and lower fuel demand, not the lexical upgrades below.
